Underground storage is more suited to large volumes and long timeframes (weeks to seasons), and has a lower operating pressure (50–250 bar). Salt caverns are spread across the globe, but some countries have limited capacity. Asia Pacific, South America, Southern Europe and the west coast of North America, for example, have few such salt caverns. For regions that do have suitable formations, however, the potential is usually vast and orders of magnitude larger than needed. Salt caverns are used for hydrogen storage in only two countries (the United States and the United Kingdom).
